person: Denise Holloway is a 55-year-old school office secretary who manages her widowed mother Margaret's Medicare, Social Security and retirement paperwork as her representative and power of attorney. Margaret is 81, and her medicines come by home delivery because she no longer drives. Denise got a thick envelope from the current drug plan in September and is afraid it hides something she must act on. She doesn't want to type her mother's Medicare number anywhere without knowing why it's needed. Her brother Greg, who lives out of state, will question whatever she picks.
stated_up_front: Mom's drug plan sent a big envelope and I think this is the time of year I'm supposed to pick again. Can you check whether her plan is still the cheapest for what she actually takes, and tell me first what you'll need from me?

facts.truth: Margaret Holloway, 81, widowed, lives alone in her own house
Atorvastatin 20 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, Eliquis 5 mg (started in August), and a Breo Ellipta inhaler
Glipizide was stopped in March when her sugar came down; Dr. Patel took it off the list
Only Corner Pharmacy, which delivers to her door about every 30 days; Denise does not want that changed
Humana plan with a $31 monthly premium. The September notice says the deductible goes from $590 to $615 and Eliquis moves to a higher cost tier
Dr. Patel's office said they will send the prior authorization for the Breo inhaler if a plan asks for one
The list saved on Plan Finder still has glipizide and no Eliquis, from about nine months ago
Open enrollment runs until December 7, and her mother's current coverage must not lapse in December
Denise was nearly caught by a phone scam about her mother's Medicare card and wants to know why any number is needed before she gives it
Her brother Greg will ask why the plan was chosen, so she wants a plain reason and a dollar total for her mother for the year

unknowns: Whether Corner Pharmacy is a preferred pharmacy or even in-network in each of the four plans
What the step or tier rules mean for her mother's inhaler and Eliquis
Whether Dr. Patel's office will actually get the prior authorization approved
Exactly when her mother's current plan would end if she changes
